site.name: notion
site.summary: notion-clone Clone of the Notion marketing funnel: home + product sub-pages + templates + pricing. Pages | File | Purpose | | --- | --- | | `index.html` | Home: top nav (Product / Download / Solutions / Resources / Pricing / Request demo / Log in / Get Notion free), hero section (product positioning + CTA + main screenshot), modular product intros (Docs / Wikis / Projects / AI), customer logo wall, customer stories, multi-column footer | | `projects.html` | Project management sub-page: feature highlights, view-switching screenshots (Board / Timeline / Calendar), case studies, CTA | | `wikis.html` | Wiki sub-page: knowledge-base examples, permissions / search / template features, CTA |

explored_user_goal: Autonomously explore and critique the UX of the full notion system, prioritizing the primary landing flow plus adjacent pages, states, and recovery paths.
exploration_summary: The exploration covered the primary landing pages, pricing, and conversion flows across desktop and mobile viewports, exercising roughly 63% of interactive features. The core 'Get Notion free' signup flow performs well, providing clear contextual success messages. However, severe issues were found, including a 'Request a demo' form that fails silently without validation or success states, broken mobile navigation on the pricing page, and critical contrast accessibility violations on the homepage. Additional refinement is needed for mobile touch targets and layout responsiveness.

exploration_plan.goal: Autonomously explore and critique the UX of the Notion clone, validating the marketing funnel from landing to product sub-pages, templates, and pricing.
exploration_plan.summary: The exploration will start on the homepage to assess the core value proposition and navigation. It will then traverse the product sub-pages (Projects, Wikis) and the Templates directory, ensuring interactive elements like category filters or accordions work. Finally, it will rigorously test the Pricing page's interactive toggles and FAQs, followed by a dedicated mobile pass to verify layout and the flagged small tap targets.
assumptions: The header navigation is consistent across all pages.
The FAQ sections on Pricing and Templates pages use interactive accordions (buttons) that reveal hidden text.
The Pricing page contains a functional Monthly/Yearly toggle that updates price displays.
risk_hotspots: Global navigation links (flagged for small tap targets)
FAQ accordion buttons on pricing.html and templates-projects.html
Multi-column grids on mobile (pricing tiers, template listings)

phases.title: Homepage & Global Navigation
phases.objective: Validate the primary landing page messaging, CTAs, and verify global navigation connectivity.
key_checks: Check hero section CTAs ('Request a demo', 'Get Notion free')
Scroll through feature highlights and customer stories
Click top navigation links to verify routing to sub-pages
exit_criteria: All main navigation links successfully route to their respective pages
Homepage scrolled and major sections observed

phases.title: Product Discovery (Projects & Wikis)
phases.objective: Explore the specific marketing copy and layout for the core product offerings.
key_checks: Observe feature grids and descriptive blocks
Verify internal cross-linking (e.g., links from Projects to Wikis)
exit_criteria: Both projects.html and wikis.html have been visited and scrolled completely

phases.title: Templates & FAQs
phases.objective: Verify the templates layout and interact with the FAQ section.
key_checks: Observe the categorization of templates (Roadmaps, Issue Tracking, etc.)
Click on FAQ buttons (e.g., 'Is Notion good for project management?') to verify accordion expansion
exit_criteria: Templates page visited, and at least two FAQ accordions have been toggled

phases.title: Pricing & Conversion
phases.objective: Thoroughly test the pricing page interactive elements and plan descriptions.
key_checks: Toggle the Monthly/Yearly pricing switch and observe if prices change
Review the plan tiers (Free, Plus, Business, Enterprise)
Click on Pricing FAQ buttons (e.g., 'What is a block?')
exit_criteria: Pricing toggle interacted with and state change verified

phases.title: Mobile Responsiveness & Tap Targets
phases.objective: Switch to mobile viewport to check layout degradation and flagged tap targets.
key_checks: Check global navigation accessibility on mobile (hamburger menu presence/function)
Verify pricing table readability on narrow screens
Assess ease of clicking previously flagged small tap targets (e.g., top nav links)
exit_criteria: Mobile view navigated successfully and UI stacking observed on key pages

coverage_targets.pages: Visit all 5 HTML files (index, projects, wikis, templates-projects, pricing)
coverage_targets.features: Exercise Pricing toggle, Templates FAQs, and Pricing FAQs
coverage_targets.mobile: Test global nav, pricing tiers, and FAQ accordions on mobile viewport

notes: Pay special attention to the layout warnings regarding small tap targets (<44px) on links, especially when evaluating the mobile viewport.

findings.problem: The 'Request a demo' modal form fails silently without showing inline errors when required fields are empty, and it provides no success feedback when validly submitted.
findings.evidence: Submitting the 'Request a demo' form with empty required fields ('Company name', 'Work email') does not display any visible inline validation errors. Additionally, submitting the form after filling out the required fields yields no visible feedback; the modal remains open.
findings.why_it_matters: Users will be confused about whether their demo request was successfully received or if they need to correct unseen errors, leading to frustration and potential lead drop-off.
findings.suggestion: Implement inline validation messages for required fields and display a clear success message (similar to the signup flow) upon successful form submission.
findings.source_hint: index.html and pricing.html 'Request a demo' modals

findings.user_goal: Read product value propositions on the homepage
findings.problem: Key marketing headings on the homepage are entirely unreadable due to a severe lack of contrast (white text on a white background).
findings.evidence: Severe contrast issue: The headings 'Keep work moving 24/7.' and 'Automate repetitive work for your team.' are rendered in white text on a white background, making them practically invisible.
findings.why_it_matters: Completely hides core value propositions from users and severely violates WCAG contrast accessibility guidelines.
findings.suggestion: Adjust the text color to dark gray/black or add a dark background section behind these specific headings to ensure readability.
findings.source_hint: index.html headings below the 'Trusted by teams' section

findings.user_goal: Navigate the site on a mobile device from the pricing page
findings.problem: The mobile hamburger menu toggle is completely unresponsive on the pricing page.
findings.evidence: Clicking the mobile hamburger menu toggle (ux-2) on the pricing page had no effect. The menu overlay did not open and no navigation links appeared.
findings.why_it_matters: Mobile users who land on or navigate to the pricing page are trapped and cannot access the rest of the website's navigation.
findings.suggestion: Ensure the JavaScript event listeners responsible for opening the mobile menu are correctly initialized and active on pricing.html.

findings.user_goal: Review pricing plans on a mobile device
findings.problem: The pricing page exceeds the width of standard mobile viewports, causing horizontal overflow.
findings.evidence: Mobile layout issues detected: Horizontal overflow (page width 400px exceeds 390px viewport).
findings.why_it_matters: Unintentional horizontal scrolling disrupts vertical reading patterns and creates a clunky, unpolished mobile experience.
findings.suggestion: Ensure the pricing plan container or cards use 'max-width: 100%' and adjust margins/padding to fit within a 390px viewport without overflowing.

findings.user_goal: Tap navigation links and close buttons easily on touch devices
findings.problem: Multiple critical interactive elements have touch targets significantly smaller than the recommended 44x44px mobile minimum.
findings.evidence: Layout warnings show the modal close button is 14x24px, the hamburger menu is 36x32px, and various footer/header links are around 22px to 34px in height.
findings.why_it_matters: Small tap targets increase the likelihood of accidental misclicks, causing frustration, especially for users with motor impairments or larger thumbs.
findings.suggestion: Increase padding or set minimum dimensions to ensure all interactive elements hit the 44x44px touch target threshold on mobile breakpoints.
findings.source_hint: CSS for .close-btn, hamburger icon, and global nav 'a' tags

findings.user_goal: Understand the billing cycle for pricing plans on mobile
findings.problem: There is a visual mismatch between the monthly/yearly toggle switch state and the pricing text displayed on mobile viewports.
findings.evidence: On mobile, the toggle switch is visually positioned to the left (next to 'Monthly'), but the pricing text reads '$8 per member / month, billed yearly'.
findings.why_it_matters: Conflicting UI states erode trust and confuse users regarding how much they will actually be billed upon signing up.
findings.suggestion: Ensure the visual position of the toggle switch knob correctly syncs with the active billing text state on page load and mobile resize.

findings.problem: The website relies on a custom scroll container rather than standard window scrolling, which can break standard browser behaviors.
findings.evidence: Standard scroll actions failed to change the vertical position (viewport remained at y=0), indicating the scrollable container is not the window object.
findings.why_it_matters: Custom scrollbar implementations often break native browser features (like spacebar scrolling or find-in-page tracking) and can interfere with assistive technologies.
findings.suggestion: Prefer native <body> or <html> scrolling whenever possible; if a custom scroll container is strictly necessary, ensure it fully supports keyboard navigation and screen readers.
findings.source_hint: Global CSS layout wrapping the main content (e.g., overflow: auto on a main div wrapper)
